newsitem.title: FRANCE: New BoF member Bernard close Chirac ally.
newsitem.headline: New BoF member Bernard close Chirac ally.

text.p: Jean-Rene Bernard, named on Friday as one of two new members of the Bank of France's council, is seen as a close ally of President Jacques Chirac but is not known to have strong views on monetary policy.
Bernard, 64, comes from the technocratic elite which traditionally rules France and has worked both in government administration and in state-sector companies.

He was a financial advisor to late president Georges Pompidou when he was prime minister in the 1960s, served abroad as an ambassador, and most recently was deputy governor of property lender Credit Foncier, which he left last year.
His son-in-law, Jean-Pierre Denis, is deputy secretary general in Chirac's office while Bernard also has close links with the president independently of family ties, political sources say.

Though he has not spoken publicly either for or against France's decade-old policy of linking the franc to the mark, political sources say he would probably be more dovish on interest rates than the two outgoing members.
Bernard and Pierre Guillen, ex-president of the CNPF employers assocation, were named on Friday to replace ex-journalist Jean Boissonnat and ex-banker Bruno de Maulde.
Sources close to the nomination process said Chirac intervened personally to get Bernard and Guillen on a list of six nominees proposed for the two positions at the nine-member council.
One source said Bernard would be likely to follow Chirac's lead in setting monetary policy.

An "inspecteur general des Finances" (inspector of finance), the top qualification for those seeking a career in France's state administration, he has also worked at oil company Elf, and was head of state-owned bank CIC from 1987 to 1989.
